items.title: Google DeepMind Unveils Gemini Robotics 2.5 for Real-World Dexterity
items.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, its most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date, on November 10. Trained with Gemini 4 Argon, it was evaluated across more than 200 real-world tasks (serving food with tongs, tying bows, liquid pipetting) and shows 30-100% higher success rates and 20-30% faster completion than prior baselines. In a Mercedes-Benz production-line proof-of-concept, Apptronik's Apollo 2 humanoid reached a 96% kitting success rate. The release also adds improved physical safety steering and the open ASIMOV-Jailbreak benchmark for robotic adversarial resistance, and is rolling out to robotics partners.
items.impact: This pushes physical AI from lab demos toward unstructured, real industrial environments. The big shift is reliability at scale plus explicit safety steerability for human-adjacent robots, signaling that embodied intelligence is becoming a deployment problem, not just a research one.

items.title: Alibaba Opens Early Access to Qwen4-Max Preview with 1M-Token Context
items.summary: On November 11, 2026, Alibaba (Aliyun) opened early access to Qwen4-Max Preview, the flagship of its new Qwen4 generation. The model accepts images and video as input and supports a context window of up to 1 million tokens. It is integrated into Qwen App, Qoder, QwenWork, and QwenStudio, and is callable via API through the Token Plan subscription, with credit consumption cut to 20% of standard rate (8% during night hours) through November 25. Alibaba emphasizes stronger coding, agentic task execution, frontend design, and world-knowledge capabilities, though it has not yet published independent benchmarks.
items.impact: This is chiefly a price-and-context attack on flagship inference where the battle for coding and agent pipelines is fought. The two-week discounted window lets teams run their own evaluations on long-context, multimodal, agentic scenarios before committing to a model.

items.title: GitLab CVE-2026-97229: Critical Unauthenticated RCE Added to CISA KEV
items.summary: CVE-2026-97229 is an integer overflow in GitLab's CI/CD regular-expression compiler that lets an unauthenticated attacker achieve remote code execution (CVSS 10.0). CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on October 29, 2026, confirming active exploitation, with a federal remediation deadline of November 1. Shadowserver reported over 1,000 internet-exposed instances remained unpatched; Alpine Linux disclosed a thwarted attempt against its own instance. Fixed in 19.2.8, 19.3.5, and 19.4.2 (and later 19.5.x), with a related CVSS 10 regex-handling RCE (CVE-2026-110264) and a dependent Ruby/Onigmo engine patch also required for self-compiled installs.
items.impact: GitLab is the control plane for source code, CI/CD, and increasingly MCP/AI pipelines. An unauthenticated RCE on self-managed instances exposes repository secrets, model artifacts, and deployment credentials. Patch immediately; GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already fixed, but self-managed and custom-Ruby deployments need both the app and engine updates.

items.title: Google's November 2026 Android Bulletin Fixes 216 Flaws, Including Zero-Click RCE
items.summary: Google's November 2026 Android Security Bulletin patches 216 vulnerabilities (23 rated Critical) across the Framework, System, kernel, and chipset components. The headline issue is CVE-2026-58868, a critical heap buffer overflow in FrameDecoder.cpp that enables remote code execution with no user interaction or elevated privileges, affecting Android 14 through 17. Two further critical zero-click RCEs appear in System (CVE-2026-58876, CVE-2026-58936). Fixes ship across two patch levels, 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-05, with the later level covering all issues plus kernel and vendor (MediaTek, Qualcomm, Unisoc) components.
items.impact: A zero-click media-processing RCE is a prime attack path for mobile fleets. Google's bulletin does not confirm in-the-wild exploitation, but enterprises must verify patch levels (aim for 2026-11-05 or later) across mixed vendor and carrier fleets, since an OS patch date alone does not cover vulnerable baseband or modem firmware.

items.title: EDPB Adopts Statement on Privacy Risks of Smart Glasses
items.summary: On October 13, 2026, the European Data Protection Board adopted a statement - accompanied by the expert report 'The connected gaze' - on the data-protection risks of smart glasses. These devices resemble ordinary eyewear but capture video and audio and run AI such as facial and object recognition, enabling near-invisible collection of bystanders' personal data. The EDPB clarifies that posting footage to public accounts makes the user a controller and that manufacturers and app providers cannot offload their GDPR obligations onto users. It recommends prominent, hard-to-disable recording indicators (LEDs, audio cues), privacy-by-design defaults (on-device processing, blurring of bystanders, geofencing), and notes valid bystander consent is difficult to obtain.
items.impact: The statement sets a de-facto EU design standard for AI wearables and signals looming enforcement by national data-protection authorities. Manufacturers and organizations deploying smart glasses must revisit recording indicators, purpose-limitation documentation, and controller-versus-processor allocation - part of tightening scrutiny on pervasive AI capture devices.
